requirements.statement: The page indicates its default language with the lang and/or xml:lang attribute, either on the html element or on every text element or one of its parents.

citations.quote: Pour chaque page web, l’indication de langue par défaut vérifie-t-elle une de ces conditions
Indication de la langue de traitement principale du document qui peut être présente sur l’élément racine html ou sur chaque élément de la page concerné via les attributs lang et/ou xml:lang

routes.statement: The html element carries the language indication, with the attribute or attributes the document type calls for: lang for HTML up to 4.01 and HTML5, lang and xml:lang for XHTML 1.0 served as text/html, xml:lang for XHTML 1.0 served as application/xhtml+xml and for XHTML 1.1.

citations.quote: L’indication de la langue de la page (attribut `lang` et/ou `xml:lang`) est donnée pour l’élément `html`
Soit au moyen de l’attribut lang sur la balise html si le code est du HTML5 ou du HTML4 ;
Soit au moyen des attributs lang et xml:lang sur la balise html si le code est du XHTML 1.0 ;
Pour XHTML 1.0 servi en "application/xhtml+xml" : attribut xml:lang obligatoire, attribut lang recommandé ;
Pour XHTML 1.1 : attribut xml:lang obligatoire, attribut lang non supporté ;

routes.statement: Every text element carries the language indication itself or through one of its parent elements.

citations.quote: L’indication de la langue de la page (attribut `lang` et/ou `xml:lang`) est donnée sur chaque élément de texte ou sur l’un des éléments parents.
Sinon, vérifier la présence d’une indication de langue sur chaque élément de texte ou l’un de ses parents.

rationale.text: The test has one requirement with two routes: the indication on the html element, or on every text element or a parent of it. The methodology and glossary say which attribute each document type needs (lang for HTML, both for XHTML 1.0 served as text/html, xml:lang for XHTML 1.1 and XHTML served as XML); the document type is known from the doctype and the served content type. Whether the html element carries an attribute is a fact of the DOM. Which texts count as a text element is not: the wording says each text element and does not say whether a field's value, text generated by CSS, an alternative text, the page title or the text of a framed document is one. So the custom check never answers no_fault through the second route. An earlier version did, after checking a list of text items, and a page with an untagged field value outside that list would have passed. The entry is fail_only, not full. full needs every accepted route to be able to pass, with a valid case per route that comes out passed (spec 10.4 point 4), and a page that meets the test only through the second route always gets cannot_tell from this check, so that route can never pass. What would raise it: a definition of the text elements of a page that code can list and show complete, cited from the official text, with the check answering cannot_tell as soon as the page holds text outside it; then no_fault through the second route, and a corpus case for it. The check faults a page whose html element has neither lang nor xml:lang in any form while a witness has no lang or xml:lang on any parent. A witness is a text node that is a text element under any reading of the wording. Then the second route fails for it whichever texts are counted, the first fails because html has no attribute, and the fault proves the test fails. A node is a witness only when it is ordinary text, visible and exposed: inside body, under plain content elements only (divs, sections, paragraphs, headings, lists, tables and phrasing such as span, em or strong), none with a role, aria-hidden, hidden or inert attribute, and none a shadow host; holding two letters in a row; present and not ignored in the accessibility tree; drawn in a generic family or a listed system text font that the page does not define itself with @font-face; with opacity 1 and no filter, mask, clip or blend on it or any ancestor; in an opaque colour that contrasts with a plain background; and with a part at least 4 pixels square inside the viewport and every clipping ancestor, not covered by another element. Every other node makes the check abstain. That rules out text that could be decorative, hidden from assistive technologies, invisible but laid out (zero opacity, transparent, clipped, off-screen, covered), or a pictogram drawn from letters: an icon font, by ligature or letter by letter, or a symbol font such as Wingdings. It also rules out text whose status as a text element is open: the name of a link, button or label, code, ruby annotations, SVG and MathML text, single letters, and text in shadow trees. An ordinary paragraph with no language source is still a witness. The cost is that a page whose uncovered text is all in web fonts, links or hidden regions gets needs review instead of failed. Everything else is cannot_tell, by stated rules: an empty attribute or one that does not fit the document type (the wording says the indication is given, and does not say whether an empty or unsuitable attribute gives it), a page without an html attribute where no witness lacks a language source, and a rendered frame whose document lacks the indication (the wording does not say whether a framed document is part of the page here). The link examines both routes for the whole page, decided or abstained on, and its fault means failure. At fail_only the tool may say failed only on an uncovered witness, and needs review otherwise; it never says passed. axe's html-has-lang is evidence only: it looks only at the html element, so a page that uses the second route gets a fault although it meets the test. axe's html-xml-lang-mismatch is tagged but not linked: it compares the base language of lang and xml:lang when both are on the html element, which says nothing about whether either route is met. Applicability is always: the test applies to every page, and the check never answers inapplicable. Needs is empty: attributes, styles, geometry and the accessibility tree are read on the page as loaded.

citations.quote: est donnée sur chaque élément de texte ou sur l’un des éléments parents
Dans chaque page web, la langue par défaut est-elle présente
Si c’est le cas, **le test est validé**.
Pour XHTML 1.0 servi en "text/html" : attribut lang et xml:lang obligatoires ;
